sources: Overcoming Gravity 2nd Edition – Steven Low (primary authority)
The Calisthenics Skill Tree template v1.6.1
meta.notes: Where sources conflict, Overcoming Gravity 2nd Ed is the authority. Progression levels: 1=Beginner, 2=Novice, 3=Intermediate, 4=Advanced, 5=Elite.
meta.session_generator_note: The terminal handstand node is 'freestanding-handstand' (not 'handstand'). The skill selector and session generator must reference 'freestanding-handstand' as the handstand tree goal node. Intermediate nodes (chest-to-wall-handstand, wall-shoulder-taps, kickup-attempts) feed the session accessory slot while the athlete progresses toward it.

nodes.name: Dead Hang
nodes.description: Passive hang from a bar with both hands, full arm extension, relaxed shoulders. Foundation for all pulling and lever work — also conditions tendons and connective tissue.
skill_specific_accessories: Bar hang with active shoulder depression
nodes.video_reference: dead hang form tutorial calisthenics scapular

nodes.name: Arch Hang
nodes.description: Active hang with a slight arch in the body and depressed, retracted scapulae. Teaches the active shoulder position required for pull-up and lever progressions.
skill_specific_accessories: Dead hang to arch hang transitions
nodes.video_reference: arch hang scapular pull tutorial bodyweight bar

nodes.name: Scapular Pull
nodes.description: From a dead hang, depress and retract the scapulae without bending the elbows. Builds foundational scapular strength and body awareness for all pulling skills.
nodes.video_reference: scapular pull tutorial calisthenics bar hang depression

nodes.name: Support Hold
nodes.description: Top position of a dip hold on parallel bars or rings with arms fully locked and shoulders depressed. Foundation for all pushing and dip-based skills.
nodes.video_reference: support hold parallel bars rings shoulder depression

nodes.name: Ring Support Hold
nodes.description: Support hold on gymnastics rings with arms locked out and rings turned out (RTO). Conditions wrists, elbows, and stabiliser muscles as the foundation for all ring pushing work.
nodes.video_reference: ring support hold RTO turned out rings tutorial

nodes.name: Ring Dip Negative
nodes.description: Controlled slow descent (3–5 seconds) from support position to bottom of dip on rings. Builds eccentric strength and joint stability before full ring dips.
nodes.video_reference: ring dip negative tutorial eccentric rings controlled descent

nodes.name: Ring Dip
nodes.description: Full dip on gymnastics rings with RTO lockout at top. Demands significant stabiliser strength not present in bar dips — a prerequisite for ring muscle-up.
nodes.video_reference: ring dip tutorial RTO lockout full range gymnastics rings

nodes.name: Hollow Body Hold
nodes.description: Supine position with lower back pressed flat, arms overhead, legs raised — creating a rigid hollow shape. The universal body tension pattern underlying all calisthenics skills.
nodes.video_reference: hollow body hold tutorial gymnastics progression core

nodes.name: German Hang
nodes.description: Hanging inverted from a bar with arms behind the body in shoulder flexion. Entry point for skin the cat and the back lever series; conditions shoulder flexibility and joint tolerance.
skill_specific_accessories: Passive German hang with feet on ground
nodes.video_reference: german hang tutorial skin the cat shoulder flexibility bar

nodes.name: Tuck Skin the Cat
nodes.description: Rotating from a dead hang through an inverted tuck into a German hang and back. Builds shoulder flexion range and the pulling strength base for back lever.
skill_specific_accessories: Slow tuck skin the cat negatives
nodes.video_reference: skin the cat tuck tutorial bar rings beginner rotation

nodes.name: Pike Skin the Cat
nodes.description: Skin the cat with straight legs in a pike position, requiring greater shoulder flexibility and hamstring length. Direct prerequisite to the back lever.
skill_specific_accessories: Hanging knee raises for shoulder flexibility
nodes.video_reference: skin the cat straight leg pike progression advanced bar

nodes.name: L-Hang
nodes.description: Hanging from a bar with legs raised to 90 degrees, parallel to the floor. Builds hip flexor and abdominal compression strength for L-sit, front lever, and muscle-up.
nodes.video_reference: L hang tutorial hanging leg raise compression hip flexor

nodes.name: Planche Lean
nodes.description: Push-up position with hands at hips, leaning forward so shoulders are well ahead of wrists. Develops straight-arm pushing strength and wrist conditioning required for planche.
nodes.video_reference: planche lean tutorial straight arm strength wrist conditioning

nodes.name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
nodes.description: Push-up with hands rotated outward and placed at hip level, shifting weight forward over wrists to simulate a planche lean. Builds wrist, anterior deltoid, and serratus strength needed for tuck planche.
nodes.video_reference: pseudo planche push up tutorial straight arm planche progression

nodes.name: Wall Handstand
nodes.description: Handstand performed with heels against a wall for support. Builds vertical pressing strength, overhead stability, and wrist tolerance before freestanding work.
nodes.video_reference: wall handstand tutorial beginner form alignment nose to wall

nodes.name: Chest-to-Wall Handstand
nodes.description: Handstand performed facing the wall with chest close to the surface. Trains proper stacked alignment (hips over shoulders over wrists) rather than the banana shape common in heel-to-wall work.
nodes.video_reference: chest to wall handstand tutorial alignment nose to wall

nodes.name: Wall Handstand Shoulder Taps
nodes.description: In a chest-to-wall handstand, shift weight onto one hand and briefly tap the opposite shoulder. Develops the unilateral balance and midline stability needed for freestanding work.
nodes.video_reference: wall handstand shoulder taps tutorial balance shift

nodes.name: Freestanding Kick-Up Attempts
nodes.description: Repeated freestanding kick-up attempts aiming to find and hold balance away from the wall. Trains the proprioceptive control and fingertip pressure management that converts wall strength into freestanding balance.
nodes.video_reference: freestanding handstand kick up attempts balance practice

nodes.name: Freestanding Handstand
nodes.description: A controlled freestanding handstand without wall support. The primary balance skill milestone; demands whole-body tension, fingertip pressure regulation, and shoulder endurance.
strength_prerequisites: 10 consecutive wall handstand shoulder taps each side
nodes.video_reference: freestanding handstand tutorial progression kick up balance control

nodes.name: Tuck Front Lever
nodes.description: Inverted hang from a bar with knees tucked to chest and back parallel to the ground. The first formal position in the front lever progression.
nodes.video_reference: tuck front lever tutorial progression bodyweight inverted

nodes.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
nodes.description: Tuck front lever with the back flat (no rounded spine) and thighs parallel to floor — more demanding due to the longer lever arm and greater lat engagement required.
nodes.video_reference: advanced tuck front lever form tutorial flat back lat

nodes.name: One-Leg Front Lever
nodes.description: Front lever with one leg fully extended and one leg tucked, reducing the lever arm relative to straddle. Bridges the gap between advanced tuck and straddle front lever.
nodes.video_reference: one leg front lever tutorial progression intermediate

nodes.name: Straddle Front Lever
nodes.description: Front lever with legs in a wide straddle to reduce the lever arm. Builds the straight-arm pulling strength needed for full front lever.
nodes.video_reference: straddle front lever tutorial straight arm pulling strength

nodes.name: Front Lever
nodes.description: Full front lever: body completely horizontal, legs together and straight, arms fully extended. One of the definitive pulling strength skills in calisthenics.
nodes.video_reference: full front lever tutorial hold progression Steven Low

nodes.name: Ice Cream Maker
nodes.description: From a dead hang, pull up while simultaneously moving into a front lever position, then descend back to hang. One of the most demanding horizontal pulling movements — requires both pulling strength and a solid front lever hold.
nodes.video_reference: ice cream maker tutorial front lever pull up combination

nodes.name: Tuck Back Lever
nodes.description: Hanging below a bar face down, knees tucked, body roughly parallel to the ground. Develops shoulder extension strength as the entry point for back lever.
nodes.video_reference: tuck back lever tutorial beginner progression shoulder extension

nodes.name: Advanced Tuck Back Lever
nodes.description: Tuck back lever with back flat and hips fully extended — the bridge between tuck and straddle back lever progressions.
nodes.video_reference: advanced tuck back lever form tutorial flat back

nodes.name: Straddle Back Lever
nodes.description: Back lever with legs held in a wide straddle, reducing the lever arm. A demanding intermediate position between advanced tuck and full back lever.
nodes.video_reference: straddle back lever tutorial progression intermediate

nodes.name: Back Lever
nodes.description: Full back lever: body completely horizontal, legs together and straight, arms extended downward. Requires exceptional shoulder extension flexibility and pulling strength.
nodes.video_reference: full back lever tutorial hold progression skin the cat

nodes.name: Tuck L-Sit
nodes.description: Support hold with both knees tucked to chest, feet off the ground. Builds hip flexor and tricep pushing strength as the entry to full L-sit.
nodes.video_reference: tuck L-sit tutorial beginner parallel bars floor

nodes.name: One-Leg L-Sit
nodes.description: Support hold with one leg fully extended parallel to floor and one tucked. Bridges the compression demand gap between tuck and full L-sit.
nodes.video_reference: one leg L-sit tutorial progression hip flexor compression

nodes.name: L-Sit
nodes.description: Full L-sit: both legs extended straight and parallel to the floor in a support position. Demonstrates significant hip flexor strength, compression capacity, and tricep endurance.
strength_prerequisites: 30s tuck L-sit on parallettes or floor
nodes.video_reference: L-sit full tutorial hold parallettes floor bars progression

nodes.name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
nodes.description: Pull-up pulled high enough that the chest contacts the bar. Builds the elevated pulling position and explosive pulling strength needed for muscle-up transition.
skill_specific_accessories: High pull-ups with pause at top
nodes.video_reference: chest to bar pull up tutorial technique height

nodes.name: Typewriter Pull-Up
nodes.description: At the top of a pull-up, slide horizontally from side to side with one arm extending, like a typewriter carriage. Develops unilateral pulling strength and shoulder adduction required for one-arm progressions.
nodes.video_reference: typewriter pull up tutorial unilateral pulling strength

nodes.name: Muscle-Up Negative
nodes.description: Slowly lowering from the top dip position down through the transition and into a dead hang. Builds muscle-up-specific pulling and transition strength via eccentric loading.
nodes.video_reference: muscle up negative tutorial transition eccentric false grip

nodes.name: Muscle-Up
nodes.description: Full bar or ring muscle-up: pulling from a dead hang, transitioning over the bar/rings, and pressing to full lockout. Combines explosive pulling strength with a technically demanding transition.
nodes.video_reference: muscle up tutorial bar rings strict technique progression

nodes.name: Tuck Human Flag
nodes.description: Holding a vertical pole with both arms and suspending the body horizontally with knees tucked. Develops the lateral pushing and pulling force required for human flag.
nodes.video_reference: tuck human flag tutorial beginner pole vertical

nodes.name: Straddle Human Flag
nodes.description: Human flag with legs in a wide straddle, reducing the lever arm. A demanding intermediate position before full human flag.
nodes.video_reference: straddle human flag tutorial progression intermediate

nodes.name: Human Flag
nodes.description: Full human flag: body held completely horizontal from a vertical pole, arms extended, legs together. One of the most visually striking and physically demanding calisthenics skills.
skill_specific_accessories: Lateral force training with bands on pole
nodes.video_reference: human flag full tutorial hold progression vertical pole

nodes.name: Tuck Planche
nodes.description: Both feet off the ground in a tuck position with arms locked straight and hips at shoulder height. The first true straight-arm planche position.
nodes.video_reference: tuck planche tutorial straight arm hold progression

nodes.name: Advanced Tuck Planche
nodes.description: Tuck planche with back flat (no rounded spine) and hips fully extended at shoulder height. Increases the lever demand on the shoulder girdle significantly.
nodes.video_reference: advanced tuck planche tutorial flat back hold straight arm

nodes.name: Straddle Planche
nodes.description: Full planche with legs held wide in a straddle, body horizontal, arms locked straight. A major milestone requiring exceptional straight-arm pushing strength.
nodes.video_reference: straddle planche tutorial progression straight arm intermediate

nodes.name: Planche
nodes.description: Full planche: body held completely horizontal with legs together and arms straight, supported only by hands. An elite-level straight-arm pushing skill.
nodes.video_reference: full planche tutorial hold progression straight arm elite

nodes.name: Wall Headstand Push-Up
nodes.description: Push-up from a headstand position against a wall. Builds overhead pressing strength specific to HSPU without yet demanding full handstand balance.
nodes.video_reference: wall headstand push up tutorial pike HSPU progression

nodes.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
nodes.description: Pike push-up with feet elevated on a box or bench, increasing the shoulder angle toward vertical. Bridges the gap between floor pike push-up and wall HSPU.
nodes.video_reference: elevated pike push up tutorial feet on box HSPU progression

nodes.name: Wall Handstand Push-Up
nodes.description: Full handstand push-up performed with heels against a wall. Develops the overhead vertical pressing strength and range of motion needed for freestanding HSPU.
nodes.video_reference: wall handstand push up tutorial form range of motion HSPU

nodes.name: Freestanding Handstand Push-Up
nodes.description: Handstand push-up performed freestanding without wall support. Requires both the pressing strength of a HSPU and full freestanding balance — an advanced convergence of skills.
nodes.video_reference: freestanding handstand push up tutorial advanced balance strength

nodes.name: Cossack Squat
nodes.description: Deep lateral squat with one leg extended to the side while the other is fully loaded. Builds hip mobility, adductor flexibility, and lateral balance needed for pistol squat.
nodes.video_reference: cossack squat tutorial hip mobility lateral squat flexibility

nodes.name: Shrimp Squat
nodes.description: Single-leg squat where the rear leg is held behind with knee approaching or touching the ground. Develops quad dominance, hip flexor mobility, and balance required for full pistol squat.
nodes.video_reference: shrimp squat tutorial single leg quad balance pistol progression

nodes.name: Assisted Pistol Squat
nodes.description: Single-leg squat to full depth with band, TRX, or pole for balance assistance. Builds single-leg strength and ankle dorsiflexion range without yet demanding full balance.
skill_specific_accessories: Assisted pistol squat with resistance band
Single-leg box squat to low box
nodes.video_reference: assisted pistol squat tutorial band TRX single leg depth

nodes.name: Pistol Squat
nodes.description: Full unassisted single-leg squat to the floor and back up with the free leg held extended forward. A complete test of single-leg strength, mobility, and balance.
skill_specific_accessories: Single-leg box squat to low box
nodes.video_reference: pistol squat tutorial full form unassisted progression

nodes.name: Tuck Dragon Flag Negative
nodes.description: Lowering from an inverted tuck position down toward horizontal while maintaining full-body tension. Eccentric-first entry to the dragon flag series — safest for connective tissue.
nodes.video_reference: tuck dragon flag negative tutorial eccentric beginner

nodes.name: Advanced Tuck Dragon Flag
nodes.description: Dragon flag held with back flat and hips extended in an advanced tuck. The intermediate step between tuck negative and straddle/full dragon flag.
nodes.video_reference: advanced tuck dragon flag tutorial flat back progression

nodes.name: Dragon Flag
nodes.description: Full dragon flag: body held rigid in a straight line from shoulders to feet, lowered and raised from a bench. An elite anterior chain exercise requiring full-body tension and lat control.
nodes.video_reference: dragon flag full tutorial bench straight body tension

nodes.name: Nordic Curl Negative
nodes.description: Kneeling with feet anchored, slowly lowering the body forward under control. The safe eccentric-first entry to Nordic curl; prevents injury while building hamstring strength rapidly.
nodes.video_reference: nordic curl negative tutorial hamstring eccentric strength

nodes.name: Nordic Curl
nodes.description: Full Nordic curl: lowering and raising the body from a kneeling position with feet anchored using only hamstring strength. Produces the greatest eccentric hamstring stimulus of any exercise.
nodes.video_reference: nordic curl full tutorial hamstring GHR strength
